extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It is designed to evaluate temporal perception and cognition in open-world video understanding using multiple-choice QA generated from public video annotations.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by selecting videos from existing benchmarks, filtering them for diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty, and then automatically converting video annotations into multiple-choice QA format using LLMs (ChatGPT) with template-based and LLM-based option generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and their annotations from 11 existing video datasets/benchmarks, with selected clips primarily ranging from 5s to 35s.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses an automatic QA generation paradigm: guided by task definitions, it converts public video annotations into multiple-choice questions. Questions are generated with ChatGPT based on the task definition, and answer options are constructed from ground-truth annotations or via LLM-based generation; options are then randomly sampled and shuffled.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports an evaluation-oriented quality check for option extraction: their prompt achieves a 100% option extraction rate, compared with MMBench's 87% alignment rate with humans. It also states that using multiple-choice format avoids biased scoring and manual intervention.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT was used to generate questions and, for some tasks, to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice QA; LLMs were also used to generate answer options and ensure similar option lengths.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is described as being limited by prior benchmarks that focus on static image spatial perception, basic video tasks, particular domains, or restricted scenes, implying potential coverage bias toward certain task types and settings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that existing benchmarks are insufficient for comprehensive temporal understanding evaluation because they focus on static images, basic video tasks, specific domains, or restricted scenes; it also notes that labor-intensive annotations make them expensive to create.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve evaluation of multimodal large language models, supporting broader understanding of open-world multimodalities and better model design.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Used as a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models on video understanding and temporal perception tasks, specifically in a question-answering formulation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR, we randomly shift the start or end points of the video clips; for QA generation, we automatically convert video annotations into multiple-choice QA format via LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We select videos from existing benchmarks, filter for video diversity and temporal sensitivity by eliminating short clips and extremely long videos, and exclude overly difficult CLEVRER questions with more than 10 conditions.
